_comment: Manifest for the self-hosted Alaska lidar DEM collection.
target_epsg: the *appropriate local UTM zone*, NAD83(2011) realization.
MatSu is delivered tagged UTM 5N but spans 150.5W - 147.0W, i.e. almost
entirely zone 6 and up to 3 degrees past the zone 5 edge. It is the one
dataset that gets a genuine zone change.
Source datum tags are honored literally (user decision, 2026-09-05):
Lower_KP and MatSu declare WGS 84, so a real WGS84 -> NAD83(2011) datum
transform is applied to them. Homer (NAD83) and KBay (NAD83(2011)) stay
in the NAD83 family. If the WGS84 tags turn out to be a vendor mislabel,
those two will sit ~1-2 m off Homer/KBay and must be rebuilt with an
max_zoom: chosen so one web-mercator pixel ~= one source pixel at that

'gated': true = keep out of the public catalog and off R2 (make_catalog skips it unless --include-gated; r2_sync excludes it); served only behind the admin login once that pathway exists (Hoonah 2015, Corax, Chugachmiut).

datasets.title: Homer 2019 bare-earth DTM
datasets.notes: Source NAD83 / UTM 5N (EPSG:26905), LZW, 128x128 blocks. No vertical CRS declared.

datasets.title: Lower Kenai Peninsula lidar DEM
datasets.notes: Source tagged WGS 84 / UTM 5N (EPSG:32605). Uncompressed and stripe-blocked (43603x1) - must be converted to a tiled COG before any windowed read. No vertical CRS declared.

datasets.title: Kachemak Bay 2023 lidar DEM
datasets.notes: Arrives as a valid COG (ZSTD, 512 blocks) in a COMPOUND CRS: NAD83(2011) / UTM 5N + NAVD88 height. Already the target horizontal zone, so the archive stage copies rather than warps - warping to a 2D EPSG:6334 would be an identity resample that also silently drops the declared NAVD88 vertical datum. It is the only one of the four that declares its vertical reference. Web tiles rebuilt 2026-09-06: the compound NAVD88 CRS made gdalwarp geoid-shift full-res reads but not overview reads (see CLAUDE.md); the archive now has GDAL-computed overviews (translate mode).

datasets.title: Matanuska Valley 2019 bare-earth DEM
datasets.notes: 82 GB SAGA .sdat, stripe-blocked. No vertical CRS declared. ELEVATIONS ARE IN FEET and are converted to metres on ingest (vertical_scale): the raw grid reads 246.1 at Palmer and 341.5 at Wasilla, whose published elevations are 240 ft and 344 ft - a metres reading would put downtown Palmer at 807 ft. Homer and Lower Kenai agree with each other in metres at an overlap point (19.84 vs 20.06), so the foot units are MatSu's alone. International foot assumed; the US survey foot differs by 2 ppm (3 mm at 1500 m), which is far below the data's own accuracy. Zone-5-tagged but lies in zone 6 - this is the one real reprojection. max_zoom 16 (1.14 m) rather than 17 (0.57 m): 17 would oversample 0.91 m source 1.6x for 4x the bytes. RENAMED 2026-09-12 (Hig): this is the Matanuska corridor; the Susitna side is the 2011 sister blocks. SOURCE FILL: the SAGA grid declares nodata -99999 but holds none; instead 84.5% of the box is exactly 0.00 in one contiguous region outside the lidar swath (a flat 0 m plateau that shaded as real ground). tools/lidar/mask_fill.py --fill 0 turns that region (the zeros connected to the raster border, dilated one coarse cell) into the declared nodata in an intermediate GeoTIFF, /Volumes/Nunatak/lidar_build/matsu_2019/source_masked.tif, which is the build source; genuine 0.00 m pixels inside the swath survive. Raw: /Volumes/Powder/Alaska GIS/Raster/AK_lidar/Matsu_2019/Bare_earth_DEM/2019_MatSu_UTM5.sdat.

datasets.title: Matanuska Valley 2011 bare-earth DTM (9 ft)
datasets.notes: Mat-Su Borough 2011 lidar (flown 2011-05-10..12), Matanuska River corridor from Palmer east to ~147.2W. ELEVATIONS ARE IN FEET (metadata: altunits feet, NAVD88 via GEOID09) and are converted to metres on ingest; max 5873 in the raw grid is 1790 m, which is right for the Chugach/Talkeetna summits here and impossible in metres. Verified against matsu_2019 at Palmer airport, Sutton and Chickaloon: 70.78/137.04/414.87 m vs 70.94/137.17/415.10 m. Lies in UTM zone 6. max_zoom 15 (2.27 m) for 2.74 m source.

datasets.title: Seward 2023 bare-earth DTM

datasets.notes: USGS 3DEP AK_GlacierBay_2019_B19, the COMPLETE delivery: 6,728 bare-earth 1 km tiles in four work units (4 and B2 at 1 m QL2, 5 and B3 at 0.5 m QL1), downloaded from rockyweb.usgs.gov to /Volumes/Nunatak/lidar_src/glacier_bay_2019/<unit>/ on 2026-09-07 (26.4 GB, all size-verified). Three tile names occur in two units (identical data). max_zoom 16 (1.25 m at 58.6N).

datasets.title: Anchorage 2015 bare-earth DTM (3 ft, MOA / NOAA Digital Coast)
datasets.notes: Municipality of Anchorage 2015 lidar (Merrick, QL2, 957 sq mi), the COMPLETE DEM as republished by NOAA Digital Coast dataset 8431: 51 GeoTIFF tiles of 10240x10240 px at 3 ft in NAD83 / Alaska State Plane zone 4 (US survey feet), NAVD88, Float32 LZW, nodata -9999, 13 GB, downloaded from https://noaa-nos-coastal-lidar-pds.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/dem/AK_Anchorage_DEM_2015_8431/ to /Volumes/Nunatak/lidar_src/anchorage_2015/ on 2026-09-11 and mosaicked with gdalbuildvrt. Elevations are in US survey feet, but the tiles DECLARE it (compound CRS '... (ftUS) + NAVD88 height (ftUS)'), so gdalwarp converts them to metres itself; no vertical_scale here. The first build (2026-09-12 overnight) applied the scale as well and shipped heights 0.3048x too small -- caught by Hig as an under-exaggerated surface; rebuilt the same day. Supersedes Hig's partial local set of 308 .img tiles. Lies in UTM zone 6. max_zoom 17 (0.57 m) for 0.91 m source.

datasets.title: Homer 2018 NCMP bare-earth DEM
datasets.notes: NOAA/USACE National Coastal Mapping Program 2018, coastal strip Homer to Anchor Point (~50 km2), merged from 1 m-grid BareEarth tiles at 0.543 m. File tagged WGS 84 / UTM 5N (EPSG:32605): PROJ treats WGS84 -> NAD83(2011) as a null shift, and a Nuth & Kaab fit against homer_2019 (2026-09-12) shows only ~0.2 m residual, so no re-tag needed. Sits +0.08 m above homer_2019. NAVD88 per NCMP convention (metadata not local). Second teacher for the Kenai 2008 reprocessing. Units confirmed metres against 3DEP (fit slope 0.99, +0.24 m).

NAD83(2011)/UTM 8N, GEOID12B orthometric heights, MAE 9.1 cm. Hydro-conditioned: water pixels set to 0 m, so the shoreline is a cliff. Already the target zone: translate. datasets.title: Juneau 2012 bare-earth DTM

datasets.title: Pedersen Lagoon 2025 multibeam bathymetry
datasets.notes: NPS Water Resources Division / Kenai Fjords NP, EchoBoat 160 uncrewed survey vessel with Norbit iWBMSe multibeam, June 10-12 2025, after the 7 August 2024 landslide-generated tsunami. Source: KEFJ_Pedersen_05m.xyz (positive-down depths, negated here). Gridded by lidar_build/bathy_src/pedersen_merge.py: cell means of the soundings at 0.5/1/2 m, chosen per 2 m block by sounding density (0.5 m where >=95% filled, 1 m >=90%, else 2 m), no interpolation. Metadata states NAVD88 GEOID12B but also that soundings were tide-corrected to MLLW: confirm the vertical datum with NPS before comparing with lidar. NAD83(2011)/UTM 6N.

datasets.title: Lituya Bay 2023 preliminary bathymetry
datasets.notes: Preliminary 2023 bathymetry of Lituya Bay, 1 m Float32 GeoTIFF, NAD83(2011)/UTM 8N, NaN nodata, -169 to +6 m. No metadata on disk: surveyor, vertical datum and processing unknown. Lituya_PrelimBathy.tif in the same folder is an RGB rendering, not elevations. GATED 2026-09-14 at Hig's request until the originator confirms provenance and vertical datum.

datasets.title: Seldovia 2019 NCMP bare-earth topobathy
datasets.notes: NOAA/USACE National Coastal Mapping Program 2019 (JALBTCX), Seldovia and Seldovia Bay: green lidar, so the grid is continuous from the hills to about -31 m. Source: the 31 vendor BareEarth_1mGrid tiles, mosaicked with a VRT (bathy_src/seldovia_2019_bareearth.vrt); tiles are NAD83(2011) geographic at 0.9e-5 deg (~1 m), warped here to UTM 5N. The companion 1mGrid tiles in the same package are the FIRST-return surface (vegetation kept, +15 m over bare earth at the 90th percentile) and are deliberately not used. Also on disk, not published: 31 classified LAS, 125 RGB orthos, NAVD88 zero contour. Public (NOAA/USACE). VERTICAL: the tiles are labelled NAVD88 but the vendor LAS headers say the heights were computed with xGEOID17B, not the GEOID12B that NAVD88 means elsewhere here, so the delivered surface sits 1.42 m low. vertical_shift_m 1.42 corrects it; see the build_lidar docstring for the evidence and the independent tide-gauge check.

datasets.title: Kachemak Bay 2008-2009 multibeam bathymetry
datasets.notes: NOAA hydrographic surveys H11933/34/35/38 (2008) and H12084-90/12114/12146 (2009), the Kachemak Bay 'Hydropalooza'. Built by bathy_proto/stitch_kachemak.py from the per-survey, per-depth-band BASE node lists (Raw/H*/*.xyz), each gridded at its own native cell size (1 m to ~23 m depth, 2 m to ~52 m, 4 m to ~115 m, 8 m below) with no search radius and no interpolation, then stacked finest-on-top into one 1 m VRT: 66 bands, unsurveyed ground left as nodata rather than triangulated across, which is what the vendor's ready-made TIFFs do (32% of one test window was fabricated that way). HORIZONTAL: the node lists carry no CRS, so the grids were written with an override; the survey metadata says NAD83, and the VRT is re-tagged EPSG:6334 without touching pixels (an earlier tag of WGS 84 / UTM 5N would have been ~1 m off in Alaska). VERTICAL: the source is MLLW. vertical_shift_m -1.38 puts it in NAVD88, measured as the median lidar-minus-bathymetry over the two NCMP topobathy surveys that overlap it (2018 Homer -1.334 m over 1.0 M cells, 2019 Seldovia -1.400 m over 2.2 M cells); NOAA Coal Point publishes -1.553 m, and per-2 km blocks run -1.30 to -1.50, so the bay's separation genuinely varies and a constant carries about +/-0.15 m. Matching the lidar is the point, since this exists to be differenced against it. Public (NOAA).

datasets.title: Woodard 2008 ground test: vendor
datasets.notes: METHOD TEST, not a survey. One 2 km patch of the Kenai 2008 point cloud (Woodard Canyon) gridded five ways so the ground filters can be compared in the difference overlay. Same points, same grid recipe, same pinned bounds; only the ground classification differs. Vendor class 2, as delivered with the 2008 survey. dev_only keeps it out of the public catalog: these are renderings of the SAME ground, and a reader meeting two of them in the survey list would think they were two surveys.

datasets.title: Woodard 2008 ground test: smrf steep
datasets.notes: METHOD TEST, not a survey. One 2 km patch of the Kenai 2008 point cloud (Woodard Canyon) gridded five ways so the ground filters can be compared in the difference overlay. Same points, same grid recipe, same pinned bounds; only the ground classification differs. PDAL filters.smrf, steep parameters: cell 1.2, slope 0.8, window 12, threshold 0.5. dev_only keeps it out of the public catalog: these are renderings of the SAME ground, and a reader meeting two of them in the survey list would think they were two surveys.

datasets.title: Woodard 2008 ground test: taught
datasets.notes: METHOD TEST, not a survey. One 2 km patch of the Kenai 2008 point cloud (Woodard Canyon) gridded five ways so the ground filters can be compared in the difference overlay. Same points, same grid recipe, same pinned bounds; only the ground classification differs. Supervised HistGradientBoosting on PDAL geometry features, taught by the 2019 surface. dev_only keeps it out of the public catalog: these are renderings of the SAME ground, and a reader meeting two of them in the survey list would think they were two surveys.

datasets.title: Woodard 2008 ground test: ptd
datasets.notes: METHOD TEST, not a survey. One 2 km patch of the Kenai 2008 point cloud (Woodard Canyon) gridded five ways so the ground filters can be compared in the difference overlay. Same points, same grid recipe, same pinned bounds; only the ground classification differs. Axelsson progressive TIN densification, angle 40, distance 3, seed 10 m. r-lidar's MIT C++ library, driven from PDAL by tools/lidar/ptd_ground. dev_only keeps it out of the public catalog: these are renderings of the SAME ground, and a reader meeting two of them in the survey list would think they were two surveys.

datasets.title: Woodard 2008 ground test: ptd, density-blended grid
datasets.notes: METHOD TEST, not a survey. One 2 km patch of the Kenai 2008 point cloud (Woodard Canyon) gridded five ways so the ground filters can be compared in the difference overlay. Same points, same grid recipe, same pinned bounds; only the ground classification differs. Same PTD ground points as kenai_woodard_ptd, gridded density-aware: the 1.75 m IDW radius where ground points are plentiful, 4 m where they are sparse, blended on the measured point count and held back from convex crests. Under dense canopy the 2008 survey leaves a median of one ground return per 1.2 m cell and 31% of cells empty, so a single slightly-high point owns its cell and the next cell is owned by another: speckle, which a hillshade turns into visible false roughness. This halves the excess.

datasets.title: Prince of Wales Island 2017 lidar DTM
datasets.notes: USGS 3DEP OPR, AK_Prince_of_Wales_Island_QL1_Lidar_2017_B17, 1705 tiles delivered at 0.5 m float32 in NAD83(2011) / UTM 8N. 5,639 km2 of real data inside 6,166 km2 of tile boxes. ARCHIVED AT 1 m, not native: at 0.5 m the archive would be ~27 GB, roughly twice the largest survey in the collection, for a survey nobody has asked for at that resolution; the 0.5 m tiles stay on disk so any area that later earns it can be rebuilt native. archive_resample average, because a 2x downsample with bilinear samples the target grid instead of integrating the source pixels it skips. HORIZONTAL: the delivery is not uniformly tagged -- 1593 tiles carry EPSG:6337, 91 carry a compound tag with NAVD88 height and 21 carry plain NAD83 from 1986. All three sit interleaved on the same unrotated half-metre lattice, so it is a tagging inconsistency, not three surveys. The VRT re-tags every tile EPSG:6337 without touching a pixel. Left alone the plain-NAD83 tiles would take a NADCON5 datum shift and the compound ones a geoid shift, putting metre-scale steps along arbitrary internal boundaries. Public (USGS).

datasets.title: Kenai Peninsula 2008 bare-earth DTM (re-classified)
datasets.product: DTM (bare earth, re-classified from the point cloud)
datasets.notes: USGS 3DEP AK_Kenai_2008 (Aero-Metric, 2008-05-21 to 09-22), 14.05 billion points at ~1.21 pts/m2. No public DTM exists for this survey anywhere, so this one is built here from the points. GROUND CLASSIFICATION: Axelsson progressive TIN densification (r-lidar's MIT C++ library, driven from PDAL by tools/lidar/ptd_ground), angle 40, distance 3, seed 10 m, outlier detection off. Chosen on a hand-scored test patch against the 2019 QL1 surface: crest loss 11.9% against the vendor classification's 20.5%, the tightest spread and fewest gross errors of six candidates, and the least false roughness under dense canopy. 3,130 tiles of 2 km with a 30 m classification buffer, 6.37 h on 8 cores, no failures. Grids are snapped to a GLOBAL 4 ft lattice: a 2 km tile is 1640.42 cells, so pinning each raster to its own tile bounds put neighbours up to 51 cm out of step and would have seamed the mosaic. Agreement with the 2019 survey where they overlap: median +0.035 m, MAD 0.095 m over 20.4 M cells. DESPIKED after gridding (tools/lidar/despike_dtm.py): two tests, because neither catches both artifacts -- an iterative 5x5-median test for the low spikes that outlier detection would have caught, and a scale-free support test for clouds and bird flocks, which asks whether a blob's lowest cell clears the 90th percentile of its own rim rather than how high it is, so a 1800 m arete survives and a blob hanging in the air does not. The classified point cloud is kept on Powder so the gridding can be redone without reclassifying. dev_only until reviewed. Public (USGS).
